Example Beispiel

Solve for \(x\) if \(3\ln x+4\log_{10} x=1\). Lösen Sie nach \(x\) auf, wenn \(3\ln x+4\log_{10} x=1\).

Solution Lösung

This has logs to two different bases. So we must first express each logarithm in terms of logs to the same base, \(e\) say Recall Dies hat Logarithmen zu zwei verschiedenen Basen. Also müssen wir zuerst jeden Logarithmus in Termen aus Logarithmen zur gleichen Basis ausdrücken, \(e\) erinnern Sie sich

\[\log_{10} x=\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln 10}.\] So \(3\ln x+4\log x=1\) becomes \[ 3\ln x+4\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln 10}=1\qquad\text{or}\qquad \left(3+\dfrac{4}{\ln 10}\right)\ln x=1\] leading to \(\ln x=\dfrac{\ln 10}{3\ln 10 +4}=\dfrac{2.302585}{10.907755}=0.211096\) and so \[ x=e^{0.211096}=1.2350311.\] \[\log_{10} x=\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln 10}.\] Also wird \(3\ln x+4\log x= 1\) zu \[ 3\ln x+4\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln 10}=1\qquad\text{oder}\qquad \left(3+\dfrac{4}{\ln 10} \right)\ln x=1\] was zu \(\ln x=\dfrac{\ln 10}{3\ln 10 +4}=\dfrac{2.302585}{10.907755}=0.211096\) führt und somit \[ x=e^{0.211096}=1.2350311.\]
